subject: general
question:
The reaction given below is an example which of the following types of reaction?

Potassium bromide(aq) + Barium iodide (aq) → Potassium iodide(aq) + Barium bromide(s)
solution:
The correct answer is **__Double displacement reaction__.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

**Double displacement reaction:**

__
 
• A double displacement reaction involves the exchange of ions between two reactants, resulting in the formation of
 two new products
 

 
• 
 
 
• In the given reaction, potassium ions (K⁺) exchange places with barium ions (Ba²⁺).
 
• This results in the formation of potassium iodide (KI) and barium bromide (BaBr₂).
 
• One of the products, barium bromide, is formed as a solid precipitate, indicating a double displacement (precipitation) reaction.
 
• The general form of a double displacement reaction is AB + CD → AD + CB.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
**Displacement reaction:**

 
 
• A displacement reaction involves one element replacing another element in a compound.
 
• This typically occurs when a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element.
 
• The given reaction involves an exchange of ions between two compounds, not the replacement of an element within a compound.
 
• A single element would have to replace another element in a compound for it to be a displacement reaction.
 
• Displacement reactions usually involve a single element and a compound.
 
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
**Combination reaction:**

 
 
• A combination reaction, also known as a synthesis reaction, involves two or more reactants combining to form a single product.
 
• The given reaction involves two reactants forming two products, not a single product.
 
• Combination reactions are also known as synthesis reactions.
 
• A+B = AB is the general form of a combination reaction.
 
• Combination reactions form one product.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Decomposition reaction:**

 
 
• A decomposition reaction involves a single reactant breaking down into two or more products.
 
• The given reaction involves two reactants, not a single reactant.
 
• Decomposition reactions are the opposite of combination reactions.
 
• AB = A+B is the general form of a decomposition reaction.
 
• Decomposition reactions break one reactant into multiple products.
